messages.text: Quick question on address changes. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0041}} just called asking to update their mailing address. They passed MFA, but do we still need anything in writing, or is the verbal OK for a low-risk member?

Verbal is fine if they pass full verification and it's a standard mailing address change. Log it in MemberCRM with the verification method you used. Send the confirmation notice to the OLD address too, that's the fraud control.
Got it. Does the notice to the old address go out automatically from CoreBanking or do I have to trigger it?
It's automatic once you save in CoreBanking, but check that the 'address change letter' box is ticked. It defaults off on the quick-edit screen. Got burned on that last month.
Ah, it was unticked. Good catch, Catherine. Fixed and re-saved.
Different one: a member walked in wanting to change address on their checking and also asked us to update the card shipping address. Is the card address separate from the member record?
Separate in CardProcessor. Member record update doesn't always flow to the plastic reissue address. Open a ticket for Ops to confirm the card file got the new one before any reissue ships.
Will do. Member has a replacement for {{CARD_NUMBER:a_00092}} pending so timing matters. I'll flag it urgent.
Heads up, teller line: someone asked to change the address for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0043}} by email only, no call or visit. Looks like it came from {{CLIENT_EMAIL:c_0043}}. I haven't touched anything.

Good call, Joseph. Don't process it. That member is flagged high risk and email alone isn't sufficient verification. Route it to Nichole, since she's their advocate, and she'll do a callback to the number on file.
Forwarding to Nichole now. Should I reply to the sender at all?
Just a generic note saying we need to verify by phone or in branch. Don't confirm anything about their accounts, including {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00097}}.

Reminder for everyone: if the member is changing phone AND address in the same session, treat it as elevated. Get a second verification factor and note it. We've seen account takeovers start that way.
Agreed. I'd add that if they changed the contact number to something like {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0041}}, make sure the callback goes to the previous number on file, not the new one.
Exactly right. I'll pin both points in the channel and update the checklist by Friday.
